```{r}
here::i_am("Charm-Prices.Rproj")
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
```


# The data only records price CHANGES: on days without a change, a station still
# sells at its last price, so we carry it forward to count every station every day.
# Limit 30 days: after that, the station has probably stopped selling/reporting.

```{r}
#| eval: false
prices_daily <- map_dfr(2021:2023, function(y)
  read_csv(here("data", "clean", paste0("prices_daily_", y, ".csv.gz")),
           col_types = cols(id = "c", fuel = "c", date = "D", price = "d")))

national_daily <- function(fuel_name) {
  prices_daily %>%
    filter(fuel == fuel_name) %>%
    complete(id, date = seq(as.Date("2021-01-01"), as.Date("2023-12-31"), by = "day")) %>%
    mutate(last_change = if_else(is.na(price), as.Date(NA), date)) %>%
    group_by(id) %>%
    fill(price, last_change) %>%                          # keep the last price until it changes
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(price), date - last_change <= 30) %>%   # ...for 30 days at most
    group_by(date) %>%
    summarise(avg_price = mean(price), n_stations = n()) %>%
    mutate(fuel = fuel_name)
}


oil <- read_csv(here("data", "clean", "oil.csv"))      

daily_national <- map_dfr(c("Gazole", "E10", "SP98"), national_daily) %>%
  left_join(oil, by = "date")

write_csv(daily_national, here("data", "clean", "daily_national.csv"))
```


#checking
```{r}
daily_national <- read_csv(here("data", "clean", "daily_national.csv"))
count(daily_national, fuel)              # 1,095 days per fuel
sum(is.na(daily_national$brent_eur_l))  
summary(daily_national$n_stations)       # stations counted per day
```
#I would like to take a look at how tthe data looks like so: 
```{r}
daily_national %>%
  filter(fuel == "Gazole") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = avg_price)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = brent_eur_l), linetype = "dashed")
```
